sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant in this interlocutory application which has been filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 151 of CPC for condonation of delay of 141 days in filing the instant misc. appeal.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the award was delivered on 28.07.2022 in the Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Case No.126 of 2019 and it took about 90 days in obtaining the certified copy.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Case No.126 of 2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Further delay was occurred in making communication by learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company to the Third-Party Hub, Ranchi of the Insurance Company.
The Investigator was deputed to verify the medical bills which consumed time in preferring the appeal.
Learned counsel for the claimants has opposed the said interlocutory application.
Considering the grounds taken in this interlocutory application, the delay is condoned and the limitation petition is allowed.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant-Insurance Company in this interlocutory application which has been filed under Order 41 Rule 27 read with Section 151 of C.P.C. to adduce into evidence the photocopy of the investigation report, bill of Medanta Hospital dated 01.09.2019 and the details of payment dated 08.07.2020 by the CCL to the claimants.

It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that a total compensation of Rs.98,20,537/- with interest @ 6% per annum has been awarded in favour of the claimants by the Motor Vehicle Claim Tribunal, Hazaribagh in Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Case No. 126/2019.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Case No. 126/2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Out of the said amount,
the appellant has deposited Rs.79,54,378/- with interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the said claim which comes to Rs.99,23,482/-.

The dispute is only with respect to Rs.18,66,195/- awarded by the learned Tribunal for the medical expenses incurred in the treatment of the deceased which was reimbursed by the CCL and suppressing this fact, the claimants made the claim behind the award, was allowed for treatment and medical expenses.

In order to buttress this plea regarding reimbursement of medical expenses,
report of the investigator is sought to be adduced as additional evidence.

Reply has been filed on behalf of the claimant, wherein the objection to adduce the additional evidence is confined to the legal issue but the factual assertion regarding the reimbursement of medical expenditure by the CCL has not been denied.

Learned counsel for the claimants has opposed the interlocutory application, it is argued that additional evidence is admissible only when the party seeking to produce it establishes that notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence it could not be produced as such evidence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced after the exercise of due diligence, at the time when the decree appealed against was passed.

Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of both sides, the main plank of the argument advanced on behalf of the insurance company is that the claimant suppressed the fact that medical expenses had been reimbursed.

Consequently, the tribunal was misled and awarded The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Srikanti Devi on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92371861/
2 compensation under the said head of medical expenses also.

sentences.text: Under the circumstance, considering the grounds taken, the interlocutory application for adducing additional evidence with regard to reimbursement of the medical bill by the CCL is allowed.

The photocopy of the investigation report, bill of Medanta Hospital dated 01.09.2019 and the details of payment dated 08.07.2020 by the CCL to the claimant, is allowed as they are relevant to decide the issue raised with regard to sustainability of compensation awarded under the head of medical expenses.
Let these documents be marked as Exhibits X/6, X/7 and X/8 for identification.
I. A. No. 3413 of 2023 stands disposed of.
M. A. No. 102 of 2023 with C. O. No. 02 of 2024
List these cases on 18.08.2025 under the appropriate heading.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Pawan/ -
